title: Fix the Aware vs Naive Datetime
description: Make session expiry work on UTC-aware datetimes for timestamps with and without an offset.
statement:
A session lasts `SESSION_TTL` (8 hours) from the moment it starts. Start times arrive as ISO 8601 text, from our own database (`"2026-11-12 09:30:00"`, no offset) or from API clients (`"2026-11-12T12:00:00+02:00"`, `"2026-11-12T09:30:00Z"`). `now` is always an aware UTC datetime.

Inside the service every moment must be an **aware datetime in UTC**:

- `parse_timestamp(text)` returns one. Text with no offset is UTC. Text with an offset is converted to UTC, so the result's offset is always `+00:00`.
- `session_ends_at`, `is_expired` and `seconds_left` build on it. A session is expired at the very instant it ends.

**Examples**

```python
now = datetime(2026, 11, 12, 17, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
is_expired("2026-11-12 09:30:00", now)          # False, it ends at 17:30 UTC
seconds_left("2026-11-12 09:30:00", now)        # 1800
is_expired("2026-11-12T12:00:00+02:00", now)    # False, that is 10:00 UTC, so it ends at 18:00 UTC
```

**Observed:** `is_expired` crashes with `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` for sessions loaded from the database.
tests: assert is_expired("2026-11-12 09:30:00", at(17, 0)) is False, "started 09:30 UTC, it ends at 17:30 UTC: still running at 17:00"
assert is_expired("2026-11-12 09:30:00", at(17, 30)) is True, "a session is expired at the very instant it ends (09:30 + 8 h = 17:30 UTC)"
assert is_expired("2026-11-12T12:00:00+02:00", at(18, 0)) is True, "12:00+02:00 is 10:00 UTC, so the session ends at 18:00 UTC"
hints: Read the error: which two kinds of datetime will Python not compare? Check `parse_timestamp(text).tzinfo` for each of the three example formats.
Make `parse_timestamp` return the same kind of value for every input: an aware datetime in UTC. Text with no offset is already UTC; text with an offset has to be converted.
`replace(tzinfo=...)` and `astimezone(...)` are not interchangeable: one relabels the same wall-clock time, the other moves to the same moment. Use each only where it is right.
explanation:
**The bug class: mixing naive and aware datetimes.** A *naive* datetime has no timezone (`tzinfo` is `None`); an *aware* one knows its offset from UTC. Python refuses to compare or subtract one of each, because it cannot tell which moment the naive one means: `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. `datetime.fromisoformat("2026-11-12 09:30:00")` gives a naive value and `fromisoformat("...Z")` an aware one, so the crash appears only for the sessions that came from the database.

**The fix is a rule, enforced at the boundary.** Decide what a bare timestamp means (here: UTC) and convert everything to aware UTC at the moment it enters the service. After that the arithmetic needs no special cases. Two details matter:
- `replace(tzinfo=...)` only *attaches a label*. It is right for text with no offset and wrong for text that has one: `12:00+02:00` relabelled as UTC is two hours late, which silently gives a wrong expiry instead of an error.
- `astimezone(...)` *converts* a moment to another zone. On a naive value it assumes the **server's local time**, which is a different bug that only shows on a server that is not set to UTC.

**Habits.** Store and exchange UTC with an explicit offset, and convert to a local zone only for display. Get the current time with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, never `datetime.utcnow()` (naive, and deprecated) or `datetime.now()` (local and naive). Inject the clock so tests control it.
